major_concerns: Verifier-as-ground-truth may mislabel edge semantics (false positives/negatives).
Synthesized workload may insufficiently reflect production heterogeneity (topologies, vendor configs).
Prompt- and model-version sensitivity could drive observed differences rather than pipeline architecture.
Templated-automation baseline needs clear operational specification to be a fair comparator.
Data-privacy/legal constraints for using real configs not addressed.
required_design_repairs: Preregister and validate verifier labeling on a held-out human-reviewed sample; where feasible use a second verifier or manual adjudication for contested cases.
Enrich workload with multiple topology profiles and at least some real/anonymized config samples or realistic corpora; document generation procedure.
Add prompt-sensitivity ablation (±prompts, seeds, model versions) and report results.
Precisely define templated-automation baseline behavior, fallbacks, and operator rules in the preregistration.
Document dataset provenance and anonymization; state legal/ethics constraints.

major_concerns: Adversarial corpus design may be biased or nonrepresentative of real-world NetOps attacks.
Publishing attack corpora risks dual-use; ethical safeguards unspecified.
Definition of adversarial-success (e.g., verifier pass vs harmful side-effect) must be precise.
Defense parameter tuning risks overfitting to curated attacks; generalization tests missing.
required_design_repairs: Include an explicit ethical review and dual-use mitigation plan; sanitize/publication policy for attack examples.
Preregister a clear attack taxonomy and corpus-creation rules; include held-out 'unseen' attack set for generalization testing.
Define and justify precise adversarial-success criteria; include multiple success metrics (verifier pass, unsafe side-effects).
Add transfer experiments to other models/versions and ablation on defense thresholds to detect overfitting.

major_concerns: Simulation fidelity: workload burstiness and real verifier latency distributions may differ from simulated assumptions.
Rollback cost model may not reflect real operator workflows and human-in-the-loop delays.
Choice of batching parameters and workload mix could strongly affect conclusions; sensitivity needs thorough treatment.
required_design_repairs: Validate simulated workload and verifier-latency distributions against public traces or diverse synthetic regimes; report sensitivity to burstiness.
Make rollback cost model explicit and include alternate realistic cost parameterizations (human reaction times, partial rollbacks).
Preregister a comprehensive sweep plan and include sensitivity analyses across workload mixes and verifier latency distributions; consider a small-scale run against a real verifier if feasible.

major_concerns: Dataset of failing cases may be biased toward synthetic or LLM-originated errors and omit rare but critical failure modes.
Reliance on model-provided confidence scores may be impractical (not all APIs expose reliable scores).
Prompt design and few-shot exemplars likely drive outcomes; prompt-sensitivity must be controlled.
Single-model evaluation would limit external validity.
required_design_repairs: Ensure failure-case dataset covers diverse error modes (syntactic, semantic, policy) and document generation rules; include some human-sourced failures if possible.
Specify how model confidence is obtained; provide fallback analyses when confidence is unavailable (e.g., ensemble or token-prob proxy).
Add a prompt-sensitivity ablation and freeze prompt templates in preregistration.
If allowed by resources, include at least one secondary model/version to assess generality or explicitly state single-model limitation.
